title: ARM Mali crash in `_uniform_set_update_shared()`
body:
### Tested versions

- Using standard Android export templates for Godot 4.5.1 stable.

### System information

Godot v4.5.1 stable - Vulkan (Mobile) - Various Android and mobile versions (see details)

### Issue description

After releasing our game Rift Riff to Google Play store (using Godot 4.5.1 stable and the standard export presets), we've been seeing a 4.19% user-perceived crash rate which falls into the Bad Behaviour threshold being above the generally accepted 1.09%. I have taken our top 4 issues (in order of most to least occurrences) and made separate issues for each of them

Each issue includes:
- 5 example crash logs: Both original and the symbolicated Result. We symbolicated the logs after the fact using the Godot_native_debug_symbols.4.5.1.stable.template_release.android and the [ndk-stack](https://developer.android.com/ndk/guides/ndk-stack) methodology
- The crash headline details from Google Console
- The device information from the 5 log examples: Device model, System on Chip, CPU and GPU.

Hopefully this is helpful - please let me know if any other information is needed!
I'll edit these posts with the links to all the other issues to keep them grouped.

This is Crash 1, which seems to occur across a variety of devices (38 different kinds):
*Update* - I just realized our 2nd most prevalent crash (Crash 2) is actually the same issue here (LocalVector::size()), with a few of Crash1bs sprinkled within. I'll just add those data points to this issue as Crash2 logs.

- Crash 1:
    - Crashes on LocalVector::size()
    - Google Console Crash Grouping info:
        -  **[split_config.arm64_v8a.apk!libgodot_android.so] Java_org_godotengine_godot_GodotLib_step**
        - SIGSEGV
    - 100+ Events
    - occurs across a variety of devices (38 different kinds)
    - Device List:
        1. **POCO duchamp (POCO X6 Pro 5G)**
            - Mediatek MT6897
            - ARM Cortex-A715 (3350 MHz), 3x ARM Cortex-A715 (3200 MHz), 4x ARM Cortex-A510 (2200 MHz)
            - 6x ARM Mali G615 (1400 MHz)
        2. **Redmi Redmi Note 14**

            - 2x ARM Mali G57 (1068 MHz)
        4. **Redmi Note 11S**
            - Mediatek MT6781V/CD
            - 2x ARM Cortex-A76 (2050 MHz), 6x ARM Cortex-A55 (2000 MHz)
            - 2x ARM Mali G57 (950 MHz)
        5. **Pixel 9 Pro**
            - Google Tensor G4
            - ARM Cortex-X4 (3105 MHz), 3x ARM Cortex-A720 (2600 MHz), 4x ARM Cortex-A520 (1950 MHz)
            - 7x ARM Mali G715 (940 MHz)
        2-1. **Galaxy Tab S9 FE+**
            - Samsung s5e8835
            - 4x ARM Cortex-A78 (2400 MHz), 4x ARM Cortex-A55 (2000 MHz)

            1. Samsung Exynos 2100
            2. ARM Cortex-A78 (3000 MHz), 3x ARM Cortex-A78 (2808 MHz), 4x ARM Cortex-A55 (2210 MHz)
            3. ARM Mali G78 (858 MHz)
        2-5. Redmi Note 12 Pro
            1. Mediatek MT6877V/ZA
            2. 2x ARM Cortex-A78 (2400 MHz), 6x ARM Cortex-A55 (2000 MHz)
            3. 4x ARM Mali G68 (900 MHz)

My observations:

- Most common issue: `LocalVector<RenderingDevice::UniformSet::SharedTexture, unsigned int, false, false>::size() const
                                                                                                                                                                 /root/godot/./core/templates/local_vector.h:76:41
                                                                                                                                                                 LocalVector<RenderingDevice::UniformSet::SharedTexture, unsigned int, false, false>::end()
                                                                                                                                                                 /root/godot/./core/templates/local_vector.h:259:26
                                                                                                                                                                 RenderingDevice::_uniform_set_update_shared(RenderingDevice::UniformSet*)
                                                                                                                                                                 /root/godot/servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp:3549:40` , and they all had similar Mali G-series GPUs. The most common one seemed to be the G57, but it prevailed on newer and older devices alike.
- However, there were a few logs that were grouped with this crash according to Google Console that had a seemingly different initial issue, involving `/vendor/lib64/hw/vulkan.adreno.so` and the subsequent `RenderingDeviceGraph::_run_draw_list_command`. These examples strictly had Qualcomm Adreno GPUs. I opened a separate issue for these, tracked [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/112158).

Other Android issues with RiftRiff:

- [Crash 1b - vulkan.adreno.so / RenderingDeviceGraph::_run_draw_list_command](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/112158)
- [Crash 3 -  RenderingDeviceDriverVulkan::_release_image_semaphore()](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/112160)
- [Crash 4 -  LocalVector::operator[]()](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/112161)

Regular members of the Godot community can request access to the Rift Riff source code if necessary. Please reach out to myself or @AdriaandeJongh
